name: capture_terminal
description: Generate a styled terminal screenshot from text lines. Uses a detected terminal palette when available (Kitty, GNOME, Alacritty, WezTerm, and others) and otherwise falls back to the configured theme. Use for CLI tutorials, command output documentation, and terminal-based guides.

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Window title shown in the terminal title bar (e.g., 'bash', 'zsh', 'git log')

arguments.name: lines
arguments.desc: Lines to render. Prefix command prompts with '$ ' (or '# ' for root) for syntax-colored prompts. Other lines are rendered as output. Maximum 1000 lines.

arguments.name: output
arguments.desc: Output filename (default: auto-generated as 'terminal-<timestamp>.png' or '.jpeg' based on SNAPMCP_FORMAT). Include extension to override format.

name: capture_code
description: Generate a syntax-highlighted code screenshot using Shiki (300+ bundled languages and 27 themes). Supports inclusive startLine/endLine ranges and optional window chrome. Ideal for code documentation, tutorials, and sharing snippets with an IDE-like appearance.

arguments.name: code
arguments.desc: Source code to render. Maximum 200KB.

arguments.name: language
arguments.desc: Programming language for highlighting. Supports 300+ bundled Shiki languages, including typescript, javascript, python, rust, go, java, c, cpp, csharp, ruby, php, swift, kotlin, sql, json, yaml, markdown, html, css, bash, dockerfile, toml, xml, graphql, and many more. Use 'text' for plain text.

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Window title shown in the title bar (e.g., 'src/main.ts', 'example.py')

arguments.name: startLine
arguments.desc: First line number to show in the gutter (1-indexed). Use with endLine to show a code range.

arguments.name: endLine
arguments.desc: Last line number to show in the gutter (1-indexed, inclusive). Must be >= startLine if both provided.

arguments.name: output
arguments.desc: Output filename (default: auto-generated as 'code-<timestamp>.png' or '.jpeg' based on SNAPMCP_FORMAT). Include extension to override format.

name: capture_browser
description: Take a screenshot of an HTTP(S) URL using headless Chromium. Uses Playwright's bundled Chromium by default; set SNAPMCP_CHROME_EXECUTABLE or the experimental SNAPMCP_CHROME_PROFILE to opt into a system Chrome or persistent profile. Explicit profile mode can send profile cookies and session state to the target site. SSRF protection is enabled by default and blocks private/local targets. Supports full-page or viewport captures.

arguments.name: url
arguments.desc: URL to capture (http/https). Private and local IPv4/IPv6 targets, localhost variants, and hostnames resolving to private addresses are blocked when SSRF protection is enabled.

arguments.name: fullPage
arguments.desc: Capture the full scrollable page (true) or the viewport (false).

arguments.name: width
arguments.desc: Viewport width in pixels (320-3840).

arguments.name: height
arguments.desc: Viewport height in pixels (240-4096).

arguments.name: output
arguments.desc: Output filename (default: auto-generated as 'browser-<timestamp>.png' or '.jpeg' based on SNAPMCP_FORMAT). Include extension to override format.

name: capture_file
description: Read a file and generate a syntax-highlighted screenshot with automatic language detection from file extension. Supports 300+ bundled Shiki languages. Requires SNAPMCP_ALLOWED_PATHS to be set for security (deny-all by default). Maximum file size 5MB.

arguments.name: filePath
arguments.desc: Absolute path to the file to capture. Must be within SNAPMCP_ALLOWED_PATHS allowlist. Symlinks are resolved to prevent traversal.

arguments.name: startLine
arguments.desc: First line number to capture (1-indexed, inclusive). Use with endLine to capture a specific range.

arguments.name: endLine
arguments.desc: Last line number to capture (1-indexed, inclusive). Must be >= startLine if both provided. Defaults to end of file.

arguments.name: output
arguments.desc: Output filename (default: auto-generated as 'file-<timestamp>.png' or '.jpeg' based on SNAPMCP_FORMAT). Include extension to override format.

name: capture_markdown
description: Render GitHub-flavored Markdown as a styled document screenshot. Supports tables, task lists, and fenced code blocks with syntax highlighting. Raw HTML is escaped, JavaScript is disabled, and external resources are blocked. Maximum input 200KB.

arguments.name: markdown
arguments.desc: Markdown content to render. Supports GFM tables, task lists, fenced code blocks, strikethrough, and autolinks. Raw HTML is escaped. Maximum 200KB.

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Document title shown in the window title bar and as H1 if not present in markdown.

arguments.name: output
arguments.desc: Output filename (default: auto-generated as 'markdown-<timestamp>.png' or '.jpeg' based on SNAPMCP_FORMAT). Include extension to override format.

name: capture_html
description: Render HTML/CSS as a screenshot in an isolated, JavaScript-disabled context. Inline styles and embedded data images are supported; scripts, frames, external stylesheets, and other external resources are removed or blocked. Maximum input 200KB.

arguments.name: html
arguments.desc: HTML content to render. Active elements, event handlers, external references, and unsafe URL schemes are removed. Inline styles, <style> tags, and embedded data images work. Maximum 200KB.

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Description for logging and window title (if window chrome enabled).

arguments.name: output
arguments.desc: Output filename (default: auto-generated as 'html-<timestamp>.png' or '.jpeg' based on SNAPMCP_FORMAT). Include extension to override format.

name: capture_diff
description: Render a unified diff with color-coded additions (green) and deletions (red). Shows file headers, hunk markers, and context lines. Ideal for PR reviews, migration guides, and change documentation. Maximum input 500KB.

arguments.name: diff
arguments.desc: Unified diff content (for example, output from 'git diff' or 'diff -u'). File headers (---/+++) and hunk markers (@@ -... +... @@) are rendered when present. Maximum 500KB.

arguments.name: output
arguments.desc: Output filename (default: auto-generated as 'diff-<timestamp>.png' or '.jpeg' based on SNAPMCP_FORMAT). Include extension to override format.

name: capture_pdf
description: Convert a URL to a print-quality PDF using headless Chromium. The complete paginated document is printed. Uses a system Chrome profile only when explicitly configured. SSRF protection is enabled by default (blocks private IPs and localhost).

arguments.name: url
arguments.desc: URL to convert to PDF (http/https). Must pass SSRF validation: private and local addresses are blocked and requests are revalidated.

arguments.name: width
arguments.desc: Viewport width in pixels (320-3840) for responsive rendering.

arguments.name: height
arguments.desc: Viewport height in pixels (240-4096) for responsive rendering.

arguments.name: output
arguments.desc: Output filename (default: auto-generated as 'pdf-<timestamp>.pdf'). Must end in .pdf.

name: capture_batch
description: Capture multiple items in a single call. Each capture is processed sequentially with its own parameters. Use for batch documentation generation (e.g., capture terminal output, code file, and browser screenshot together). Maximum 10 captures per call.

arguments.name: captures
arguments.desc: Array of captures to process. Each capture specifies its type and type-specific parameters.

arguments.name: output
arguments.desc: Output directory (default: SNAPMCP_DIR). Captures saved as individual files.

name: capture_sequence
description: Capture ordered process steps as individual image files and optionally compile them into a GIF. Each step has typed capture parameters plus stepNumber and label. When GIF output is requested, frames are rendered as PNG. Maximum 60 steps.

arguments.name: steps
arguments.desc: Array of steps to capture. Each step specifies its capture type, type-specific parameters, plus optional stepNumber and label.

arguments.name: compileGif
arguments.desc: Compile frames into an animated GIF (requires at least 2 steps)

arguments.name: frameDelay
arguments.desc: Frame delay in milliseconds for GIF (10-5000). Default 800ms.

arguments.name: loop
arguments.desc: Whether the GIF loops infinitely

arguments.name: output
arguments.desc: Output directory (default: SNAPMCP_DIR). Steps saved as individual files, GIF as sequence-<timestamp>.gif

name: capture_gif
description: Create an animated GIF from 2-60 sequential captures. Frames are rendered as PNG, compiled into a GIF, and removed after encoding. loop=true repeats forever; loop=false plays once. Maximum canvas 8192x8192.

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Name for the GIF (used in default filename)

arguments.name: captures
arguments.desc: Array of frames to capture. Each frame specifies its capture type and type-specific parameters. Minimum 2, maximum 60 frames.

arguments.name: frameDelay
arguments.desc: Frame delay in milliseconds for GIF (10-5000). Default 800ms.

arguments.name: loop
arguments.desc: Whether the GIF loops infinitely (true) or plays once (false)

arguments.name: output
arguments.desc: Output filename (default: auto-generated as '<title>-<timestamp>.gif'). Must end in .gif

name: capture_document
description: Create a document with embedded step-by-step captures. Each capture is rendered as an image and embedded in the document with optional captions. Output formats: markdown (with image references), html (self-contained with base64 images), pdf (print-quality), pptx (editable PowerPoint deck), or docx (editable Word document). Maximum 30 captures per document; 25 MB per embedded image and 75 MB total.

arguments.name: title
arguments.desc: Document title

arguments.name: captures
arguments.desc: Array of captures to embed. Each specifies capture type, type-specific parameters, and optional caption.

arguments.name: format
arguments.desc: Output document format: markdown (image refs), html (self-contained), pdf (print-quality), pptx (editable PowerPoint), docx (editable Word)

arguments.name: includeTimestamps
arguments.desc: Include capture timestamps in the document

arguments.name: output
arguments.desc: Output filename (default: auto-generated as 'document-<timestamp>.md/.html/.pdf/.pptx/.docx'). Extension should match format.

name: snapmcp-hint
description: Find the right snapmcp tool by natural-language intent, or get concise setup, security, sandbox, agent, and token guidance. Use when tool selection is unclear or before loading the full documentation.

arguments.name: topic
arguments.desc: Legacy named topic: init, doctor, browser, themes, output, security, sandbox, gif, document, batch, tokens, agents, discovery, or code-mode.

arguments.name: query
arguments.desc: Natural-language intent to search, such as 'website screenshot', 'animated before and after', 'pdf export', or 'read a source file'.
